title: And If Someday
text:
And if someday the air comes good

and everything lights up,

nothing can be hoped for.


The heart itself refuses flight.

pain weighs more than joy.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's blunt refusal of consolation.

title: I Contemplate
text:
I contemplate

the cold mountain,

the slow peace,

the summit...


Yet I would return

to walk

the same road,

to love the same land

deep and dispossessed,

passionately

the same uncertainty.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the quiet turn from contemplation back into uncertainty.

title: Words
text:
Precious stones for meaning,

diamonds of reality.


If they go in dreams they lose their shine,

their luminous truth.


Living words, let no one touch them

who does not know how to care for them.




1966
editorial_note: The translation preserves the brief caution around living words.

title: Since Childhood I Dreamed
text:
Since I was small I dreamed

of being the poet

who would explain to children the history of birds;

how in them life becomes passionate,

thins, is fulfilled,

and in the skies sings itself.




1949
editorial_note: The translation keeps the vocation of explaining birds as life singing itself.

title: Silence
text:
I cannot speak; though I wanted to

I cannot speak with joy.

What am I to say? Not even

can I present a clean page.

I cannot speak, only shadows would grow

over the cursed grass.

I must be silent, but I would give

my life.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the pressure between enforced silence and the offered life.

title: Words of Paul Celan
text:
But still he could see you, an echo

that would fall groping

with the antenna of words, back

of separation.


His softly resigned face,

the lamp that would burn;

but suddenly there rises

inside me a flame

in which you whisper with pain. No. Never.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Celan-like broken image of words as antenna and separation as a back.

title: You Have Grown, Root
text:
You have grown, root,

in the body, in the hands,

in me like a part

visible of myself,

in the feverish chest like a palpable dream.


Those dark fears

of the blood

suddenly left their lair,

my life, face to face, and the gleam

of an endless dream.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the root as a visible inner growth and a palpable dream.

title: In a Single Desire
text:
The years that were lost are here, now.

The dreams I have lived grow between my hands.

I feel how so many days and beings have passed,

so many things by my side without my seeing them.

But suddenly everything returns and gathers in memory,

and so many lives

in a single desire today I have found.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the long recovery of years into one present desire.

title: The Book
text:
This book does not exist.

Pages that would inhabit

the void absurdly. I remember

—the association is not evident—

the crazed bird

flying, flying again over the sea

unable or not knowing how to alight,

it turned in the void,

flew within itself

Are words life or do they go against life?




1974
editorial_note: The translation keeps the bird image and the book's self-canceling question.

title: High Stars Without Answer...
text:
High stars without answer,

also dark passing,

life perhaps also questioning.


(For this absence I suffer, I suffer

its presence was yours and was ours.)


Something shines without end, but not you stars,

while anxiously I ask...

Death shines blinding

in the air that barely

is a gentle whisper.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the address to unanswering stars and the blinding shine of death.
